newsitem.title: USA: MCI,Telefonica, BT in strategic pact.
newsitem.headline: MCI,Telefonica, BT in strategic pact.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana, MCI Communications and British Telecom said on Friday they formed a strategic alliance to take advantage of growth opportunities across three continents and to leverage complementary strengths.
Under the deal, MCI and Telefonica's international unit Telefonica Internacional SA would form a 50-50 Pan American joint venture, managed by Telefonica Internacional, MCI said.
The venture, to be called Telefonica Panamericana-MCI, would pursue opportunties in the Latin American communications market, valued at $36 billion, MCI said in a statement.
This market was expected to grow to over $60 billion by 2000, MCI said.
Telefonica Panamericana-MCI would be well positioned to take advantage of the ongoing privatization trend in the Latin American region, MCI said.
Telefonica Internacional and MCI would set up a Pan American network to provide customers integrated global communications services, including voice, data, Internet/intranet and video, MCI said.
Telefonica Internacional would also have exclusive rights to offer Concert Communications Services products, MCI said.
On November 3, British Telecom and MCI announced plans to merge, forming a new company called Concert. They said they expect to complete the merger by the autumn of 1997.

Telefonica Internacional already operated communciations companies in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru and Puerto Rico and had holdings in the United States and elsewhere in Latin America, MCI said. MCI said it had a presence in 17 countries in that region.
MCI said Telefonica would also have the opportunity to invest in Avantel, a joint venture between MCI and Banamex, the leading financial group in Mexico.
This would enable Telefonica to participate in the Mexican communications market, estimated at $7 billion and seen doubling within the next five years, MCI said.

Telefonica and MCI Systemhouse would also form systems integration joint ventures to provide systems outsourcing and integration services to business and government customers throughout Latin America, MCI said.
The companies said in a joint statement they were also considering extending their alliance to make Telefonica the exclusive provider of Concert Communications Services' offerings in Spain.
To back the alliance, Telefonica would take about a one percent stake in British Telecom and BT would take about a two percent stake in Telefonica, the companies said.
The consideration for each investment was expected to be around $450 million, MCI said.

They were also considering extending the pact to have Telefonica Internacional SA and MCI merge their existing activities in Puerto Rico on a 50-50 basis, MCI said.n of Telefonica, joining the Concert board,

In the United States, the companies would explore the opportunity of including an agreement for MCI and Telefonica to provide customized products, promotions and marketing programs aimed at the U.S. hispanic community, MCI said.
Telefonica said it would also explore opportunities for investing with BT in Europe.

As for board representation, they were exploring extending their alliance to include Juan Villalonga, chairman of Telefonica, joining the Concert board, and Sir Iain Vallance, chairman of BT, joining the Telefonica board, MCI said.
MCI Chairman Bert Roberts said: "We are pleased to be joining with Telefonica as we expand our scope of operations to offer premier communications services to customers around the world."
